title: Renters' Rights Act: an overview for landlords
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 1 May 2026, England. Assured periodic tenancies replace ASTs; Information Sheet by 31 May 2026; no rent before the agreement is signed; no discrimination against people with children or on benefits; pet requests refused only for a valid reason; adverts show an asking rent and bidding is illegal; rent increases by Form 4A with at least 2 months' notice, once a year, challengeable above open market rent; section 21 abolished; section 8 notice usually 4 months, shorter for some grounds; selling or moving-in ground not in the first 12 months; arrears ground mandatory at 3 months' rent owed; deposit must be protected or returned before possession; rent repayment orders up to 2 years' rent.

title: Renting is changing: guide for landlords
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated government campaign page linked from GOV.UK. Changes took effect 1 May 2026; rent in advance limited to one month; tenants give two months' notice; written information duties; database rollout from 15 December 2026 starting in the West Midlands; ombudsman, Awaab's Law and Decent Homes Standard for private renting 'in the future'.

title: Implementing the Renters' Rights Act 2025: our roadmap for reforming the private rented sector
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 13 November 2025. Phase 1 on 1 May 2026; database from late 2026; landlord ombudsman membership expected 2028; Decent Homes Standard for private renting proposed for 2035 or 2037 and not confirmed; Awaab's Law for private renting date to be confirmed; council investigatory powers from 27 December 2025; maximum civil penalty rises from 30,000 to 40,000 pounds from 1 May 2026.

title: Register your rental property service: guidance for landlords
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 29 October 2026. Regional three-month registration windows from 15 December 2026 (West Midlands) to 14 November 2027 (South West), London 15 July to 14 October 2027; fee 65 pounds per property per year, pro-rated during rollout; penalties up to 7,000 pounds for not registering and up to 40,000 pounds for false information or repeated breaches; the landlord starts registration; agents can add tenancy and safety information; further information due within 28 days.

title: Extending Awaab's Law to private rented tenancies and to licences (consultation)
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 9 October 2026, closes 18 December 2026. Awaab's Law for private renting is a proposal under consultation, not yet in force, with no start date.

title: Assured tenancy forms
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 30 April 2026. Prescribed forms for private assured tenancies from 1 May 2026, including Form 3A (section 8 notice) and Form 4A (new rent); do not change the wording; notices served before 1 May 2026 need a court claim by the earlier of the notice's validity or 31 July 2026.

title: Evicting tenants (England)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Assured periodic tenancies: section 8 notice, then a standard possession order, then a warrant for bailiffs; harassment and illegal eviction can be criminal offences; separate guidance for Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

title: Tenancy deposit protection
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Three government-backed schemes in England and Wales; protect within 30 days of receiving the deposit; return within 10 days of agreeing the amount; disputed money stays protected until resolved; holding deposits need protection once the person becomes a tenant; deposits on assured periodic tenancies must be protected.

title: Tenancy deposit protection: information landlords must give tenants
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Information due within 30 days of receiving the deposit: address, amount, how it is protected, scheme and dispute service contacts, landlord or agent contacts, any third-party payer, reasons for keeping money, how to get it back, what to do if the landlord can't be reached or there is a dispute.

title: Tenant Fees Act 2019: guidance (withdrawn)
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2019 guidance on permitted payments and deposit caps was withdrawn on 8 May 2026 and points to the Renters' Rights Act guidance. Used only to say the old guidance is out of date; no deposit cap is stated in this kit.

title: Renting out your property: landlord responsibilities
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Keep the home safe and free from health hazards; gas and electrical safety; EPC; deposit protection; Right to Rent checks in England; smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; council HHSRS enforcement notices; mortgage lender permission.

title: Renting out your property: making repairs
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Landlord repairs structure, sanitary fittings, heating and hot water; at least 24 hours' notice to enter, immediate access in emergencies; tenants can claim in small claims for repairs under 5,000 pounds or ask the council for an HHSRS inspection; rent abatement for disruptive works.

title: Private renting: your landlord's safety responsibilities
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Annual gas safety check by a Gas Safe registered engineer; copy of the record before move-in or within 28 days of the check; smoke alarm on each storey; carbon monoxide alarm in rooms with a solid fuel appliance; escape routes and fire-safe furniture.

title: Electrical safety standards in the private rented sector: guidance
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 1 November 2025, England. Electrics checked at least every 5 years by a properly qualified person; tenants given proof of inspection and testing.

title: Check your tenant's right to rent
supports: Opened with WebFetch. England only; check all adults aged 18 and over before a new tenancy, not only people you suspect; time-limited permission checked within 28 days before the start; exempt accommodation list; page notes rules changing on 1 May 2026.

title: Landlord registration (Scotland)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 1 April 2025. Register before letting; renew every 3 years; letting unregistered is a criminal offence with fines up to 50,000 pounds; adverts show the registration number and EPC rating. Used as the 'other UK nations differ' example.

title: The Fair Housing Act
publisher: US Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 22 June 2023. Protected characteristics (race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability); covers landlords; complaints to HUD or court. Used because hud.gov returned 403 to WebFetch.

title: 42 U.S. Code 3604: discrimination in the sale or rental of housing
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Statute text: refusing, unequal terms, discriminatory notices and adverts (3604(c)), false unavailability, and disability rules including reasonable modifications and reasonable accommodations (3604(f)(3)).

title: 42 U.S. Code 3603: effective dates and exemptions
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Exemptions for some owner-rented single-family homes and owner-occupied buildings of up to four units; the advertising rule in 3604(c) still applies to both.

title: Using consumer reports: what landlords need to know
supports: Opened with WebFetch; guidance dated July 2023. Permissible purpose; adverse action notice required even if the report played a small part, with the reporting company's contact details, a statement it did not decide, and the right to dispute and get a free report within 60 days; credit score disclosure; secure disposal; blanket criminal-record bans may breach the Fair Housing Act.

title: Real estate disclosures about potential lead hazards
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 27 May 2026. Housing built before 1978: pamphlet, known information, records and a Lead Warning Statement before the lease is signed; keep signed copies 3 years; exemptions include leases of 100 days or less and zero-bedroom units without young children.

title: Residential Tenants' Rights Guide
publisher: New York State Office of the Attorney General
supports: Opened with WebFetch; guide date not shown. New York example of state rules: deposit up to one month's rent, returned within 14 days with an itemised statement; 30, 60 or 90 days' notice of large rent increases or non-renewal by length of tenancy; late fee only after 5 days and capped at 50 dollars or 5%, whichever is less.

title: Topic no. 414, Rental income and expenses
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 24 September 2026. Advance rent is income when received; a kept security deposit is income; repairs versus improvements; Schedule E reporting.

title: Buildium pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plans Essential, Growth and Premium; 14-day free trial; Open API on Premium; AI features (Lumina); no MCP server mentioned.

title: AppFolio pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plans Core (50-unit minimum), Plus and Max; Realm-X AI; read-only API on Plus and read/write API on Max; no MCP server mentioned.

title: Landlord Studio pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free Go plan and paid Pro and Pro Plus; US and UK; rent collection, maintenance tracking and screening (tenant pays on Go); Xero and bank feeds on paid plans; no API or MCP mentioned.

title: TurboTenant pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free, Essentials and Pro self-management plans plus a managed service; applicants pay screening fees by default; rent payments, applications, leases and maintenance requests; no API or MCP mentioned.
